title: SYSK Selects: What's with the Winchester Mystery House?
summary: A Halloween-themed SYSK Spooky Selects rerun of the 2013 episode on the Winchester Mystery House in San Jose, California. The hosts cover Sarah Winchester's background as heir to the Winchester Repeating Arms fortune, the death of her daughter Annie and husband William, her visit to a Boston medium who told her the family was cursed by spirits of people killed by Winchester rifles, and the nonstop construction that followed under foreman John Hanson. They describe the house's odd design features (stairs to nowhere, doors opening onto drops, two mirrors), its innovations (wool insulation, push-button electric lights, the annunciator call system), the 1906 earthquake's effect, her seclusion and charity, her death, and the estate auction. The episode ends with a listener mail about plotting sexual orientation and intensity on a coordinate plane.
rerun_of: How the Winchester Mystery House Worked

segments.title: Spooky Selects intro and Halloween banter
segments.summary: Josh introduces the episode as a Halloween Spooky Selects pick from 2013. The hosts banter about candy corn and their Halloween edition.

segments.title: Introducing the Winchester Mystery House
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the Winchester Mystery House in San Jose, its uncertain number of rooms, and its origins on rural land that later became suburbs.

segments.title: Sarah Winchester's background and family tragedies
segments.summary: Sarah Pardee, born in New Haven, Connecticut, married William Winchester, heir to the Winchester Repeating Arms fortune. Their daughter Annie died in infancy, and William died fifteen years later at age forty three.

segments.title: Medium's curse and the decision to build
segments.summary: Grieving, Sarah visits Boston medium Adam Coons, who tells her the family is cursed by spirits of people killed by Winchester rifles and that she must build a house endlessly to appease them. She moves west to California and buys land near San Jose.

segments.title: Seances, construction routine, and paying workers
segments.summary: Sarah conducted nightly seances in the Blue Room, received instructions, and navigated a maze of tricks meant to lose spirits. Construction ran around the clock with workers paid double, and rooms were often built and torn down.

segments.title: Odd design features and the 1906 earthquake
segments.summary: The house has switchback stairs, stairs to nowhere, doors opening onto drops, and hidden passages. The 1906 earthquake trapped Sarah in a room, after which she sealed off damaged rooms, including the front entrance, and lived on a houseboat for a time.

segments.title: House statistics and Sarah's innovations
segments.summary: The house has many fireplaces, chimneys, windows, and doorways, and only two mirrors. Sarah is credited with wool insulation, push-button electric lights, outside window shutter cranks, drip pans, and the annunciator servant call system.

segments.title: Death, estate auction, and tourist attraction
segments.summary: Sarah died in her sleep, construction stopped, and her estate was auctioned over six weeks. The house became a tourist attraction, and a documentary, Mrs Winchester's House, is recommended.

segments.title: Listener mail on sexuality coordinate plane
segments.summary: Listener Paul of Uniontown, PA suggests plotting sexual orientation and sexual intensity on a coordinate plane rather than a single line. The hosts agree and sign off.
